name: Pallof Press
description: The Pallof press is an anti-rotation core stability exercise that challenges the ability to resist rotational forces rather than produce them. Performed with a resistance band or cable anchored to the side, the exerciser extends the arms in front of the chest and holds against the pull — requiring the entire core to contract isometrically to prevent rotation. It is a cornerstone of lumbar rehabilitation, athletic performance, and functional core training.

execution.starting_position: Anchor a resistance band at chest height. Stand perpendicular to the anchor, far enough away to create tension. Hold the band with both hands at the chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Anchor the band at a door frame or rack at chest height. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, perpendicular to the anchor.
steps: Step 1: Hold the band with both hands pressed against the sternum. The band pulls horizontally toward the anchor point.
Step 2: Brace the core firmly. The feet, hips, and shoulders should all face straight ahead (perpendicular to the anchor).
Step 3: Slowly press the hands straight out in front of the chest, fully extending the arms.
Step 4: Hold for 2–3 seconds at full extension, resisting the pull of the band.
Step 5: Return the hands to the chest with control. Repeat for reps, then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale and brace as the arms extend. Breathe steadily in the hold position.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso toward the anchor — the goal is to prevent this rotation entirely
Feet shifting or hips rotating — maintain a stable square stance
Holding the breath excessively — learn to breathe while maintaining the brace
safety_considerations: Use very light resistance initially — the demand on the core is high relative to the apparent load
Safe for most low back pain populations — often one of the earliest core exercises reintroduced in lumbar rehab
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension and return. The range of motion is straightforward — the challenge is in preventing rotation throughout.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-second press out, 2–3 second hold, 2-second return. 10–15 reps × 2–3 sets per side.
coaching_cues: Squeeze your core like someone is about to punch you
Your body should look the same at full extension as at the start — no rotation
Press straight out from the sternum
